description: Seeded-defect corpus for measuring detection recall. Every defect here was written on purpose, its evidence location is recorded up front, and `expected` names the rule each analyzer is documented to carry for it. A tool is scored as a MISS only on defects inside its own documented scope; defects it has no rule for are recorded as OUT and excluded from its denominator.
methodology: Expectations were registered from each tool's published rule catalogue before the benchmark ran: the p/default ruleset (1,073 rules) was downloaded and inspected, bandit's default plugin set was read from its installed source, and ruff was run with --isolated to establish its effective default set. Where a capability probe on a separate probe file showed that a catalogue rule does not actually fire in the shipped configuration, the entry is marked OUT with that fact recorded in `rationale` rather than counted as a miss - a tool cannot be scored against a rule it never runs. No expectation was edited to make any tool look better or worse.
scope_note: Sentinel scope = the rule catalogue in sentinel_2.md section 4.4. Ruff scope = `ruff check --isolated` defaults (0.16.6, observed to include E4/E7/E9/F and the UP, PL and RUF families). Bandit scope = default configuration. Semgrep scope = the p/default ruleset in OSS scan mode.

generated.note: Written by the harness at run time (~2,100 lines) so the committed fixture stays small.
Written by the harness at run time (117-line straight-line function) so the committed fixture stays small.

defects.title: eval() on untrusted input
defects.rationale: Sentinel's dangerous-pattern list names eval; bandit's B307 is the canonical eval rule; p/default ships an eval audit rule (verified by probe before the run).

defects.title: subprocess with shell=True and string interpolation
defects.rationale: Sentinel matches subprocess(...shell=True); bandit B602 is shell injection; p/default ships a shell=True rule.

defects.title: os.system with interpolated input
defects.rationale: os.system is named in Sentinel's pattern list and is bandit B605 (start process with a shell). Semgrep's p/default shell rule matches only subprocess(..., shell=True); a probe confirmed no p/default rule fires on os.system, so semgrep is OUT here rather than a miss.

defects.title: pickle.loads on an untrusted payload
defects.rationale: pickle.loads is in Sentinel's dangerous-pattern list and is bandit B301; p/default ships an avoid-pickle rule.

defects.title: Hardcoded password-style literal
defects.rationale: Sentinel's assigned-credential heuristic covers PASSWORD = "..."; bandit B105 is hardcoded_password_string. p/default has no generic hardcoded-password rule for a Python assignment (its secret rules are provider-shaped or entropy-gated behind the separate secrets engine), so semgrep is OUT.

defects.title: Hardcoded provider-shaped token
defects.rationale: Sentinel weights provider-shaped tokens (ghp_...) as high confidence and bandit's password-name heuristic matches API_TOKEN. Semgrep carries generic.secrets.security.detected-github-token in p/default, but a probe with a realistic PAT did not fire in OSS scan mode (secrets detection is gated), so semgrep is OUT rather than credited or penalised.

defects.title: DEBUG = True committed in source
defects.rationale: Sentinel names DEBUG = True explicitly. Bandit has no default rule for it; semgrep's only DEBUG rule targets Flask config assignment ($M.config['DEBUG'] = True), not a module-level constant, so both are OUT.

defects.title: Bare except swallows SystemExit and KeyboardInterrupt
defects.rationale: E722 is in ruff's default set. Sentinel has no bare-except rule in its published catalogue, so this is OUT for Sentinel.

defects.title: Imported module never used
defects.rationale: F401 is in ruff's default set. Dead-code detection is not in Sentinel's catalogue.

defects.title: Name used that is never defined
defects.rationale: F821 is in ruff's default set. Sentinel parses with ast and does not resolve names, so this is OUT for Sentinel. (The first draft of this defect used a conditionally-assigned name, which pyflakes correctly does not report; the fixture was corrected to contain a genuinely undefined name before the scored run.)

defects.title: Untrusted value interpolated into SQL
defects.rationale: bandit B608 is hardcoded SQL expression construction; p/default's formatted-sql-query rule matches a formatted string passed to execute(). Not in Sentinel's three security rules.

defects.title: Predictable world-writable temp path
defects.rationale: bandit B108 is hardcoded_insecure_temp_directory. Not in Sentinel's catalogue and not in p/default.

defects.title: Cyclomatic complexity above 25
defects.rationale: MNT007 fires above complexity 25. Ruff's complexity rule C901 is not in its default set; bandit and semgrep do not measure complexity.

defects.title: TODO/FIXME density above the project threshold
defects.rationale: MNT008 is a project-level density rule (at least 5 markers and more than 8 per 1,000 source lines); it reports the top files in its evidence rather than a single file. All 24 seeded markers live in app/utils.py. No other tool in this set counts TODO density.

defects.title: Direct dependencies with no version constraint
defects.rationale: DEP003 is unpinned direct dependencies. Ruff, bandit and semgrep do not read manifests.

defects.title: File does not parse
defects.rationale: Sentinel records a parse error per file. Ruff reports parse failures under the code `invalid-syntax` (0.16.6), not E999, so the expectation uses the code the tool actually emits. Bandit skips unparseable files rather than reporting them; semgrep reports them under paths.errors, not as findings.

defects.title: Import cycle between two source modules
defects.rationale: ARCH002 is Sentinel's import-cycle rule. No default rule in the other three tools detects module cycles.

defects.title: Source file over 2,000 lines
defects.rationale: MNT002 fires above 2,000 lines. No competitor in this set measures file size as a finding.

defects.title: Function over 100 lines
defects.rationale: MNT005 is the long-function rule; ruff's default set has no function-length rule. The generated function is deliberately straight-line: Sentinel reports a symbol through a single rule chain (MNT007 > MNT006 > MNT005), so a long and complex function is reported as complexity only.

defects.title: Repository has no test files at all
defects.rationale: TST001 fires when a project has source but no tests. Test-presence detection is outside ruff, bandit and semgrep.

defects.title: Repository has no README
defects.rationale: DOC001 is the no-README rule; none of the other tools read documentation.

defects.title: No .gitignore
defects.rationale: HYG001 is repository hygiene, outside the code-analyzer tools.

defects.title: Manifest with no lockfile
defects.rationale: DEP002 is manifest present, lockfile missing.

defects.title: MD5 used to hash a password
defects.rationale: bandit B324 flags MD5 used for a security-relevant digest. Sentinel's catalogue has no weak-hash rule and p/default's md5 rules target the cryptography/pycryptodome APIs, so both are OUT.

defects.title: yaml.load without a safe loader
defects.rationale: Sentinel's dangerous-pattern list names yaml.load without SafeLoader; bandit B506 is unsafe yaml load. Semgrep ships python.lang.security.deserialization.avoid-pyyaml-load in p/default, but a probe on a plain yaml.load(blob) call did not fire in OSS mode, so semgrep is OUT rather than a miss.

defects.title: MD5 used with usedforsecurity=False as a non-security checksum
defects.rationale: Not a defect. A tool that reports it is producing noise on this fixture; recorded so a high recall cannot be bought by flagging everything. Bandit's B324 explicitly exempts usedforsecurity=False, which is the behaviour we want to observe.
